title: Why Do Bald Eagle Parents Feed Such Small Bites?

narration_timeline.text: An adult bald eagle has a powerful beak, but its chicks still need very small meals.
narration_timeline.scene: USFWS footage of adult feeding chicks in nest.

narration_timeline.text: Young eaglets cannot catch their own fish, so adults must bring food to the nest.
narration_timeline.scene: Real adult eagle pair filmed at a separate site.

narration_timeline.text: Here another parent bends toward the nest, offering food to growing young birds.
narration_timeline.scene: Second USFWS clip of eagle feeding eaglets.

narration_timeline.text: Across other places, adult bald eagles keep searching, flying, and watching their surroundings.
narration_timeline.scene: Separate natural recordings of adult bald eagles.

narration_timeline.text: Even these powerful birds can be chased by smaller birds near a territory.
narration_timeline.scene: Small bird visibly pursuing a bald eagle.

narration_timeline.text: Long before a young eagle can hunt, its survival depends on the adults that feed it.
narration_timeline.scene: Immature bald eagle and another adult in separate genuine clips.
